speaker: Doctor
text: GREETING: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing hematuria and right flank pain; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me how severe the pain is and if it radiates to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The combination of visible hematuria, right flank pain, and a history of recurrent UTIs in a 42-year-old male is highly suggestive of a renal calculi, which can cause secondary irritation or infection leading to these symptoms.
